what: Why not just treat competing events as censoring?
title: Getting Started: Competing Risks Pipeline
text: Suppose event interest relapse, patients die unrelated cause first. Treating death ordinary censoring standard KM Cox analysis implicitly assumes patients gone relapse eventually, lived – assumption can never check usually don’t believe. fit_competing_risks_pipeline() instead estimates cumulative incidence directly, keeping subjects risk set correct (subdistribution) timescale. event coding different . fit_km_pipeline() fit_coxph_pipeline() want binary 0/1 event indicator. function wants event_var encode event happened: 0 = censored, 1 = event interest, 2 = competing event, .

what: Why not just fit each gene separately?
title: Getting Started: RNA-Seq Mixed Model Pipeline
text: traditional approach RNA-seq differential expression – separate negative binomial GLM per gene – treats every gene told nothing gene. fit_rnaseq_nb_pipeline() instead fits one multilevel model across genes , gene-level random slope effect interest. Genes little data (noisy counts) get pulled (“shrunk”) toward population-average effect; genes strong, consistent evidence keep estimate. partial-pooling idea behind lme4/brms random effects, applied differential expression. code: set.seed(1) n_genes <- 20 n_samples <- 16  dat <- expand.grid(   gene   = paste0("gene_", seq_len(n_genes)),   sample = paste0("sample_", seq_len(n_samples)),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) dat$condition <- factor(rep(   rep(c("control", "treated"), each = n_samples / 2), n_genes )) # a handful of genes get a real treatment effect; the rest are noise responsive_genes <- paste0("gene_", 1:4) dat$mu <- ifelse(   dat$gene %in% responsive_genes & dat$condition == "treated",   80, 40 ) dat$count <- stats::rnbinom(nrow(dat), mu = dat$mu, size = 4)  fit <- fit_rnaseq_nb_pipeline(   data          = dat,   gene_var      = "gene",   count_var     = "count",   condition_var = "condition",   sample_var    = "sample",   chains = 4, iter = 2000, warmup = 1000,   cache_file = "rnaseq_vignette_fit.rds" )  fit

text: event_var means something different fit_km_pipeline() fit_coxph_pipeline(). treat event_var binary indicator (1 = event, 0 = censored). must encode event type occurred: 0 = censored (whatever cencode set ), 1 = event primary interest, 2, 3, ... = competing event types preclude event interest ever happening (e.g. death another cause event interest relapse). Reusing plain 0/1 binary indicator silently treats every non-event competing risk type... none, just reduces single-event case – wrong, usually meant ask. reason dedicated model matters: fitting standard Cox model treats competing events ordinary censoring overestimates event interest's cumulative incidence, implicitly assumes subjects experienced competing event gone experience event interest lived. Fine-Gray model avoids assumption keeping competing-event subjects risk set subdistribution timescale instead removing .
